reason: The NEON transpose is a distinct way to reduce conversion work in the measured TB path, but the poor TB scores do not show that conversion caused the regression. The 288-byte scratch stride is in bounds and tests a distinct layout; the prior 272-byte layout was not promoted, and neither cache benefit nor causality is established. Four-step unrolling is a distinct extension of the unpromoted two-step result; the paired evidence for that result was mixed. The proposed K-pair tile schedule may alias the earlier unpromoted two-step unroll, so require a clearly different instruction schedule before implementation. Half-band scratch adds packing and changes traversal, which resembles an unpromoted traversal. TA adds a timed transpose while retaining generated packing and adds A packing. Fused transpose repeats A-tile conversion across all 16 column panels, making it the highest-work, highest-risk proposal.
